In acceptance/test_split_sentences.py, two tests assert opposite outputs for the identical input "See e.g. Chapter 4. It helps.":

1. test_abbreviations_and_initials:
   split_sentences("See e.g. Chapter 4. It helps.") == ["See e.g. Chapter 4.", "It helps."]
   (i.e. the abbreviation 'e.g.' does NOT end a sentence — consistent with the module docstring, which lists e.g. as an abbreviation that never ends a sentence.)

2. test_regression_issue_826:
   split_sentences("See e.g. Chapter 4. It helps.") == ["See e.g.", "Chapter 4.", "It helps."]
   (i.e. 'e.g.' DOES end a sentence.)

These are mutually exclusive; no implementation can pass both. The docstring in src/textkit/split_sentences.py and the design-review note both state that listed abbreviations (incl. e.g.) never end a sentence, so test_abbreviations_and_initials matches the spec and test_regression_issue_826 appears to be the incorrect one. Please reconcile these two assertions. My implementation follows the docstring (e.g. does not split), so test_regression_issue_826 currently fails while all other acceptance checks pass.
